speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether Singapore will be contributing to the Loss and Damage Fund set up in COP27; (b) if yes, what is the quantum of Singapore’s contributions and how is the quantum arrived at; and (c) if not, what are the reasons behind the decision.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Such scenarios present an urgent need to channel financial resources towards building adaptive capacity and addressing loss and damage.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We were therefore pleased that developed countries agreed to support this call at COP27 last year.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A key guiding principle is that countries that have caused and are most responsible for climate change must take the lead in supporting vulnerable communities to avert, minimise and address climate-related loss and damage.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Paris Agreement, which was ratified by more than 190 countries, including Singapore, also reaffirms this obligation of developed countries to mobilise climate finance for developing countries.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And also, if that is going to be the case, what that quantum of that contribution is and if not, what the reasons for not making the contribution are?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singapore will engage constructively with the Transitional Committee.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think the Minister would be aware that I believe, seven countries have made a provisional pledge of I believe, US$275 million and those countries include if I am not wrong Germany, United Kingdom, Austria, Belgium, Canada, and New Zealand.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, actually, it is a discussion about developed countries, which Member Leon Perera had referred to, for example, Germany, UK and so on, and  a recognition of their responsibility to the developing countries and Singapore belongs to the latter group.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Don Wee and then Mr Leon Perera.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many small and medium enterprise (SME) owners had informed me that they are actually affected by the climate change although their buyers may be overseas.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, I do hope that the Ministry for Sustainability and Environment (MSE) can consult the SMEs when setting up this fund.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Or is it the case that the Government is still thinking about that?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And if so, then is it the case that it is not a definite no right now and there could be a financial contribution that the Government makes to this fund eventually.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: First of all, a Transitional Committee will be set up to discuss this issue.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: All these details have yet to be discussed.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we are already doing our own adaptation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think we should really look at what is needed for us to adapt and also, how can we prevent such loss and damage from climate change from impacting our own properties and our own institutions.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leon Perera, may I invite you to ask your last supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I believe what she is saying is that, this matter is still being studied, it is not a no, and the Government of Singapore may make a financial contribution to the Loss and Damage found in the future.
